title: Step-by-Step Environment Chain Trace Across a Block
description: Trace how each statement in a small block-structured program creates frames, adds local bindings, updates outer variables, and exits a block.

steps.description: Lines 3-44 define `Environment`, where `__repr__` (lines 40-44) formats the entire chain from the current frame outward as `name:{vars} -> parent_name:{vars}`.
Inside `trace_program()`, lines 49-56 create `glob = Environment(name="global")` and run `glob.define("total", 0)` and `glob.define("n", 5)`, printing `global:{'total': 0, 'n': 5}`.

Line 58 enters the block by creating `inner = Environment(parent=glob, name="inner")`, line 61 defines `i = 1` in `inner`, and line 65 executes `inner.assign("total", inner.lookup("total") + inner.lookup("i"))`.

Look at line 65: `inner.lookup("total")` walks up to `glob` (`0`), `inner.lookup("i")` reads `inner` (`1`), and `inner.assign("total", ...)` writes the sum `1` back into the frame where `'total'` was defined.

steps.question: After exiting the block on line 69 (`glob`), what does `glob.lookup('total')` on line 72 return, and what happens when line 76 calls `glob.lookup("i")`?
steps.answer: `glob.lookup('total')` returns `1` because `inner.assign` updated `'total'` in `glob`, while `glob.lookup("i")` raises `NameError: undefined variable 'i'` because `'i'` was defined only inside `inner`.

steps.description: Lines 68-80 print `glob` after block exit, confirm `glob.lookup('total')` is `1`, and catch the `NameError` from `glob.lookup("i")`.
At trace step 66 on line 65, `inner` is about to look up `'total'` and `'i'` and call `inner.assign("total", 1)`.
